prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which established moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: Having read the opening ballots, I now put magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first, ahead of my own opening first choice (IceCube). It is the case I like best on my own criteria: a prediction from a simple continuum model (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) that nature then confirmed in a striking way, since the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle showed that the flat band was real and that it hosts strongly correlated physics. Five of six members who ranked it put it in their top three, including a theorist-leaning, an experimental and an astro-oriented voice, which is a much broader base than my IceCube ranking has. The phenomenon has been reproduced by many groups and carried into TMD and other moire systems within a few years, so the discovery does not depend on the unsettled pairing mechanism. The theory-plus-experiment trio is a clean allocation within the supplied names and a natural three-person prize.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing. The work is under a decade old, the origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and sample-to-sample variation is large. I have said in print that elegant theory without clues from nature should not be trusted, and the same caution applies to a young field whose long-term importance is not yet shown; big ideas can take a long time to show their worth. There is also a real attribution problem: the first author of the 2018 experiments, Yuan Cao, and earlier continuum-band theory work are outside the credited names. If the committee finds that gap unacceptable, a more mature candidate such as the optical lattice clock (B061) or the IceCube discovery (B009) is the safer choice.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube first for the same reason I did, an instrument-driven window on the universe, and notes that the individual source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) have limited significance and no independent confirmation from another detector, while the collaboration credit is hard to split.
responses.response: I agree with the reservation and it is the main reason I have moved IceCube from first place to an alternative. The diffuse flux is secure, but the source identification is still thin, and I said in my own ballot that most of the flux is unexplained. Where I still disagree with you is on the value of that incompleteness: a discovery that opens a window does not need every source identified. I would keep B009 alive as the first alternative, and I would like the committee to hear a view from outside our own field on whether the Halzen and Spiering pairing is defensible against the AMANDA and Baikal founders before we drop it.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks twisted bilayer graphene second and calls the timing slightly early because the pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram are unsettled, and he prefers the topological insulator candidate (B019) as mature and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously, but I would separate the discovery from the interpretation. The flat band, the correlated insulator and the superconducting dome were seen and then reproduced by independent groups, and that is what a prize would cite. The pairing mechanism is a follow-up question, as it was for the cuprates. On B019 I am less convinced than you: Kane and Mele and Molenkamp is a fair trio on paper, but you yourself note that the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D topological insulator work sit outside the credited names, and that makes the allocation weaker than for B013, where the prediction and the experiment sit inside the trio.

responses.point: Olsson ranks twisted bilayer graphene first on the clarity and rapid reproduction of the signatures, while noting the first author of the experimental papers is not credited and that earlier theory may complicate priority. She also proposes Hosono alone for the iron-based superconductors.
responses.response: We agree on B013, and I share your worry about the omission of Yuan Cao, though the prize rules and the supplied names leave us with the group leader. Your suggestion that Hosono alone is the clean choice for B012 is a useful correction to my own ballot, where I credited three people: the first discovery at 26 K is Hosono's, and the later increases to 43-55 K are important but are improvements. That makes B012 a weaker candidate in a three-person form than I had assumed, and I would not combine it with another part.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the optical lattice clock first as a precisely defined measurement advance with clear priority for Katori and Ye, mature and reproduced across continents, and with the redefinition of the second in view.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing case and I ranked it only sixth, so I should explain why. I agree it is mature, cleanly attributed and well reproduced. My hesitation is the one Lindroth and Mehlig also raise: it sits close to the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes, and the specific new clue from nature is a better instrument rather than a new phenomenon. Your broad support persuades me to treat it as my second alternative rather than a low-ranked one, and if the committee prefers certainty over novelty, B061 is a prize I could accept without hesitation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards a field under a decade old, with an unsettled superconducting mechanism, as mature enough.
Whether omitting Yuan Cao and earlier continuum-band theorists from the credited names is acceptable, or whether it undermines a fair attribution.
Whether the IceCube source identifications will gain independent confirmation, which would change the standing of B009.
My knowledge of the priority chronology in twisted bilayer graphene and of the IceCube founders is from memory and has not been verified.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B013, B009 or B061. I have Princeton and Uppsala ties and co-authors in string theory and cosmology, none of which are connected to these candidates.
